title: Bacteria

questions.q: What are the four phases of bacterial growth?
questions.answer: The four phases are the lag phase, the log phase, the stationary phase, and the death phase.

questions.q: What is the lag phase of bacterial growth?
questions.answer: The lag phase is the first phase of growth, a period of slow growth when cells adapt to the high-nutrient environment and prepare for fast growth, with high biosynthesis rates.

triples.o: period of slow growth when cells are adapting to the high-nutrient environment and preparing for fast growth

questions.q: What is the log phase of bacterial growth?
questions.answer: The log phase, also known as the logarithmic or exponential phase, is the second phase of growth marked by rapid exponential growth.

triples.o: phase marked by rapid exponential growth

questions.q: What is the stationary phase of bacterial growth?
questions.answer: The stationary phase is the third phase of growth, caused by depleted nutrients, in which cells reduce metabolic activity, consume non-essential cellular proteins, and transition from rapid growth to a stress response state.

triples.o: third phase of growth caused by depleted nutrients
increased expression of genes involved in DNA repair, antioxidant metabolism and nutrient transport

questions.q: What is the death phase of bacterial growth?
questions.answer: The death phase is the final phase where the bacteria run out of nutrients and die.

questions.q: What is the growth rate (k) during the log phase?
questions.answer: The growth rate (k) is the rate at which cells grow during the log phase.

questions.q: What is the generation time (g) during the log phase?
questions.answer: The generation time (g) is the time it takes the cells to double during the log phase.
